column2: Description
The high-level functional area in SAP where the issue occurred (e.g., FI, MM, SD). Helps categorize the error by business domain.

This is the SAP application component (technical classification) like LO-VCH, PPM-CF, BC-CST-EQ.it's the official SAP component hierarchy used in OSS/support. A more specific sub-area within the application component. Provides finer classification of where the error belongs.

Also known as package. Indicates the technical grouping of the object (program/module) in the SAP repository. Useful for identifying ownership or transport grouping.
ABAP package (e.g., SENQ, INM_CPPM, VCH_HL_CORE). Indicates ownership and transport layer.
Date when the dump/error occurred.
The server/host name where the error (dump) was triggered.
Represents the error type or severity indicator of the Error
Time when the dump/error occurred (paired with E2E_DATE).
The SAP user ID under which the program was running when the dump occurred.
A brief description of the error (similar to the short text seen in ST22 dumps). Gives a quick idea of what went wrong.
The ABAP exception class or name that was raised (if applicable). Useful for debugging object-oriented errors.Empty for classic runtime errors like RFC or TIME_OUT.
The ABAP program or report in which the dump occurred. (e.g., SAPLSENA, SAPLRPM_FICO_INT_DATA, CL_VCH_HL_ENGINE_FACTORY======CP).
ABAP runtime error ID (e.g., UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION, CALL_FUNCTION_OPEN_ERROR, TIME_OUT). This matches ST22 dump category exactly.This is key for root cause analysis
The exact timestamp of the dump in UTC format. Useful for cross-system correlation and logs comparison.
Unique identifier of the transaction/session during which the error occurred.it's usually a technical transaction/session identifier (GUID-like or LUW ID)

Update context (*E* indicates error context) - failed update
*E*	Error context		Update failed and ended in error
*U*	Update context 		(normal)Standard update task execution (no error).
*V*	V1 update		High-priority update (synchronous update task). 
*W*	V2 update		Low-priority update (asynchronous). Often statistical/log updates.
*D*	Dialog context		Update triggered directly in dialog process (rare).
*B*	Background context	Update triggered from a background job.
*L*	Local update		Local update (SET UPDATE TASK LOCAL). Executes in same work process.
*R*	Restarted update	Update that was restarted after failure (via SM13).

Update status (1 = failed update)
Value	Meaning				Explanation
0	Initial / Not yet processed	Update request created but not yet executed.
1	Error (Failed update)		Update terminated with error → appears in SM13 failed updates.
2	Successfully processed		Update completed successfully.
3	In process			Update currently being processed by update work process.
4	Terminated (manually or system)	Update was stopped/cancelled before completion.
5	Auto-restart / Retry state	Update scheduled for restart after failure.
6	Restarted successfully		Previously failed update, now successfully reprocessed.
